learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Generalised Slowing.
Apply Generalised Slowing to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Excess diffuse theta/delta or slowed background may reflect encephalopathy, sedating medication, metabolic disturbance or drowsiness.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Severity is judged by frequency, continuity, reactivity and clinical state. Serial change can be more informative than a single recording.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Useful in delirium, toxic-metabolic states and monitoring recovery.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Diagnosing encephalopathy from a drowsy outpatient recording without clinical correlation is unsafe.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Generalised Slowing?
options: Excess diffuse theta/delta or slowed background may reflect encephalopathy, sedating medication, metabolic disturbance or drowsiness.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Excess diffuse theta/delta or slowed background may reflect encephalopathy, sedating medication, metabolic disturbance or drowsiness.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Generalised Slowing?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Generalised Slowing?
options: Diagnosing encephalopathy from a drowsy outpatient recording without clinical correlation is unsafe.
quizBank.explanation: Diagnosing encephalopathy from a drowsy outpatient recording without clinical correlation is unsafe.

reviewPrompts.answer: Severity is judged by frequency, continuity, reactivity and clinical state. Serial change can be more informative than a single recording.
Useful in delirium, toxic-metabolic states and monitoring recovery.
Diagnosing encephalopathy from a drowsy outpatient recording without clinical correlation is unsafe.
Diffuse slowing is a physiological sign, not an aetiological diagnosis.
